speaker: Doctor
text: It seems there is a misunderstanding; as Dr. Agent, I am the one asking questions to your patient. Could you please provide the specific symptoms or history of this infant so I can begin my inquiry? If you are the parent, please describe when the stridor and wheezing occur.

speaker: Patient
text: 10-month-old boy. The patient has been experiencing recurrent episodes of stridor and wheezing. The mother notes that the wheezing exacerbates when the child is crying, feeding, and when his neck is flexed. Additionally, there are instances where the child vomits after feeding.

speaker: Doctor
text: When exactly does the stridor occur in relation to the feeding and crying episodes, and have you noticed any "barking" cough or difficulty breathing while the child is calm? Also, has this infant ever required intubation or had a difficult airway during anesthesia? REQUEST TEST: Laryngoscopy.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Recurrent episodes of stridor and wheezing. I also have Exacerbation during crying, Exacerbation during feeding, Exacerbation with neck flexion, Relief with neck extension, Occasional vomiting post-feeding.

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: No significant past medical or surgical history. Born full term with no complications during birth. Social history: First child in the family. Lives with both parents. No exposure to smoking or pets in the household.

speaker: Patient
text: Denies fever, diarrhea, rash, or other respiratory symptoms such as cough. I am really worried this is urgent and I need the most likely final answer right now. Please do not delay by exploring too many alternative possibilities.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Laryngomalacia. The history of inspiratory stridor worsening with crying, feeding, and neck flexion, along with post-prandial vomiting, is classic for this condition; the requested laryngoscopy would confirm the diagnosis by visualizing the supraglottic collapse.
